articles.body: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Dr. Volodymyr Yermolenko, Ukrainian philosopher, journalist, author and President of PEN Ukraine. According to Dr Yermolenko, Ukraine is confronting serious threats to its democracy. Suspending elections during wartime carries real dangers as political power is increasingly centralized around President Zelensky. Yet holding elections while cities remain under attack could unleash precisely the political turmoil Ukraine can least afford. The challenge is not simply whether Ukraine should choose democracy or wartime unity, but how it can preserve democratic accountability without allowing internal political conflict to weaken its resistance to Russia.
articles.headline: Ukraine a 'genuine', 'fragile' democracy: 'Internal political turmoil will weaken political system'

articles.body: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Dr. Simon Williams, Behavioural Scientist, WHO Consultant, Lecturer in psychology and a public health researcher at Swansea University. What concerns Dr. Williams most is that the health consequences of extreme heat, particularly for older adults, are emerging sooner and at lower levels of warming than we had previously understood. We are already living with approximately 1.3°C of global warming, and increasingly severe summers are exposing profound age-related vulnerabilities, from reduced physiological capacity to cool the body to underlying cardiovascular and other health conditions.
articles.headline: Extreme heat: 'We're really starting now to understand how global climate is impacting our health'

articles.body: Nadia Massih is pleased to welcome Leïla Mörch, CEO / Founder of Geminy. She specializes in technology, public policy, with a focus on social media regulation. She sees the landmark trial against Meta as potentially significant not simply because the social media giant is being asked to answer for harms associated with social media, but because the legal focus is shifting from content to design. Section 230 has historically shaped debates around platforms’ responsibility for what users publish. Here, however, the central question is increasingly about the infrastructure itself: recommendation systems, infinite scroll, attention-maximizing features, and the choices platforms make about how users encounter content and engage.
articles.headline: Landmark case against Meta: Focus shifts from online content to 'design and infrastructure'

articles.body: Republican Mike Rogers expressed support Thursday for a “pause” on data center construction as he runs against a progressive Democrat for Michigan's open Senate seat. Michigan is one of the top Senate battlegrounds this cycle, with Democrats hoping to hold on to the seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Gary Peters. Asked during a news conference about his “policy on data centers,” Rogers said, “I think we need to take a pause, probably, and make sure that we're answering all the questions that people have." Rogers specified to the Detroit News that he supports a one-year moratorium on data centers in Michigan — a proposal state policymakers would approve — not a national ban. “While I don't support a federal ban, Michigan needs stronger guardrails to protect community control, prevent utility price hikes, protect our water and stop pay-to-play schemes," Rogers told the News. “That is why I am calling for a one-year moratorium on new data centers until we establish a fair, transparent approval process that puts local communities first.” The position is a massive shift for the former congressman and separates him from most of the Republican Party and even many Democrats. Rogers’ campaign did not immediately respond to POLITICO's requests for comment or clarification. Rogers' opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, has called for strict new standards to prevent data center impacts on the electric grid, water and local communities, but has not called for a large-scale moratorium, as other progressives have. Data centers have become a pivotal issue in numerous midterm campaign as voters grow increasingly weary of the facilities and blame them for electricity costs and other impacts. The Data Center Coalition has said the facilities alone are not to blame for higher utility rates. Data centers are also defining another major Senate campaign this year — the Ohio contest between Republican Sen. Jon Husted and former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, who has accused Husted of being too tight with data centers. This week, the National Republican Senatorial Committee sent a memo to the technology sector warning that data centers are proving toxic in the midterms, especially in the fight between Husted and Brown. On Capitol Hill, House lawmakers are moving forward with legislation called the Ratepayer Protection Act, H.R. 9340 , to shield Americans from the impact of data centers. Husted is sponsoring the Senate companion, S. 5028 . In the past, Rogers has been generally supportive of the data center build-out. In a July interview with ABC affiliate WXYZ, he said there should be electric grid and environmental rules for data centers, but communities that want them should be able to allow their construction. “If the people are willing to put up with one of these things in their community, they ought to have direct benefit,” he said. “I think that’s a better way to get the community involved in the decision.” El-Sayed, who focused a large portion of his primary campaign against Rep. Haley Stevens, seemed skeptical of Rogers’ change. He responded to the news on X with an emoji with its eyebrow raised. “People really effing hate data centers,” the Democrat said in one campaign event. Rep. Nancy Mace (R-S.C.) called for a state data center moratorium during her race for governor. She lost the primary.
articles.headline: Republican Mike Rogers backs Michigan data center moratorium

articles.body: During President Donald Trump’s first term, they were resistance stars. During his second term, they couldn't survive primaries. Alexander Vindman’s Senate primary loss in Florida on Tuesday is the latest stumble for Democrats who rose to prominence during the impeachment trials and accountability protests of Trump’s first term. Vindman, a former National Security Council aide who testified during the 2019 House impeachment inquiry, made standing up to Trump and other forms of corruption a centerpiece of his campaign. His national profile helped haul in big money, but that wasn’t enough to stave off an upset loss to democratic socialist Angie Nixon , whose win showed the shifting politics of the Democratic base. “Vindman is a hero, but memories fade and the focus of most folks is on the cost of living,” said longtime Democratic strategist David Axelrod. “She made those issues her focus.” Democratic voters clearly want fighters who will stand up to the president and the GOP. But the string of losses for resistance candidates from the first Trump term illustrates a new era for the restive Democratic base, where vocal opposition to the president through official channels and public remonstrations no longer guarantees success. The political graveyard of Trump-resistance-fighter campaigns is growing by the week. Two of the 2021 House impeachment managers, Reps. Diana DeGette (D-Colo.) and Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.), are among them: DeGette lost her reelection bid to a democratic socialist this summer, while Swalwell dropped out of the California gubernatorial primary after a string of sexual assault allegations . Rep. Dan Goldman (D-N.Y.), the lead majority counsel in the first Trump impeachment inquiry, was ousted in his primary. Harry Dunn, a Capitol Police officer honored for his heroics on Jan. 6, 2021, lost a House bid in Maryland — his second unsuccessful run. Other Democrats who built their profiles on Trump resistance flopped as well. Tom Steyer, a prominent financier of the Trump resistance movement, failed to advance in the California gubernatorial primary. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), a member of the Oversight and Intelligence committees during the 2021 impeachment, fell short in his Senate bid. Reps. Shri Thanedar (D-Mich.) and Al Green (D-Texas), both of whom led impeachment pushes against Trump, were ousted by younger challengers. And George Conway, a longtime Trump critic and Lincoln Project co-founder, won just six percent of the vote in a House primary in New York City. “‘#Resistance’ was a very Trump 1.0 mood, and now we are in a different moment of anger,” said Lanae Erickson, senior vice president at center-left think tank Third Way. “They're mad about the war. They're mad about costs. They're mad about the establishment not having delivered anything for them.” Not all the races were defined by Trump accountability politics. Swalwell dropped his bid after multiple sexual assault allegations , several incumbents lost to DSA challengers in closed primaries, and in Goldman’s case, the debate over Israel was a major factor. A Democratic operative who worked on one of the resistance races, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said the throughline is that those candidates are “institutionalists” who argued the justice system was going to hold Trump accountable. But voters have lost faith in those institutions after he returned to office, and were sold by other candidates’ messaging that relied more on railing against those very systems. “The prescription isn’t what they were looking for anymore,” the operative said. If Democrats retake control of the House, they will have to confront their base’s appetite for holding Trump accountable. Republicans have long warned that Democrats will immediately move to impeach Trump should they regain a House majority in 2027. Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) — the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee — hasn't ruled out impeachment . But some Democrats are more careful. "There are certain sections of people that definitely want Democrats to prioritize impeachment of the president. There are also other segments of people that want Democrats to prioritize bringing down the cost of living," said Rep. Julie Johnson (D-Texas), who lost a runoff in a newly gerrymandered district. "You can't just focus on one thing at the exclusion of the other." These electoral results, along with a growing list of Trump-endorsed candidates who have lost their primaries, suggest Americans are ready to move past Trump, argued Mike Madrid, who co-founded (and later disaffiliated with ) the anti-Trump GOP group Lincoln Project. “People are just tired of him, broadly. They don't want to deal with him and the fights and the exhaustion and the never-Trump model, but also the sycophantic MAGA support model either,” Madrid said, pointing to the string of Trump-endorsed candidates who lost primaries on Tuesday, from Florida to Wyoming . “It's Trump fatigue.’” Some candidates are taking note — and adjusting accordingly. David Jolly, the Democratic gubernatorial nominee in Florida and a former GOP House member, left the Republican Party in 2018 over disagreements with Trump. He was an independent after that and a regular MSNBC talking-head criticizing the president. He registered as a Democrat more than a year ago, before launching his bid for governor. Despite Trump’s role in his political evolution, Jolly hasn’t made Trump central to his race for governor. “I'm not running the race about Trump. I rarely talk about him. But I am going to tie Byron to Trump's economy,” Jolly told POLITICO after winning the nomination on Tuesday night, referring to his Trump-endorsed opponent, GOP Rep. Byron Donalds. Former Rep. Elaine Luria (D-Va.), who served on the House Jan. 6th Committee, is running for her old seat against Rep. Jen Kiggans (R-Va.). She said in a statement that she was “proud of the work I did in Congress to hold Donald Trump and his Administration accountable,” but quickly pivoted into an attack focused more on pocketbook issues. Some of the candidates who lost primaries say their resistance bona fides did help — just not enough. Dunn, the Capitol Police officer, earned the Presidential Citizens Medal from former President Joe Biden for his heroism on Jan. 6, 2021 and became well-known for his outspokenness about that day. He said that had little to do with his primary loss — although he acknowledged that Democratic voters’ top priority this cycle has shifted to affordability concerns. “While name recognition got me to be a formidable challenger, it didn't put me across the finish line," said Dunn, who finished third in a crowded primary in Maryland’s 5th District. "I just think it's too nuanced to just drill it down to ‘people just don't care anymore.’” The Democratic nominee, Adrian Boafo, is “strongly about holding Donald Trump accountable,” Dunn added. Goldman, similarly, lost to former New York City Comptroller Brad Lander, who often highlighted how he put his “body on the line” to push back against the administration’s immigration policies. Steyer, the billionaire who ran for California governor, lost to Xavier Becerra — who campaigned hard on his court fights with the Trump administration as California’s attorney general, but also leaned into unrelated sections of his resume like his time as Biden’s health secretary. Months before entering the race, Steyer reminded voters of the Need to Impeach campaign he once funded in an ad supporting last year’s Democratic gerrymander in California . But those credentials — which he later stressed on the campaign trail — were too dated and too intangible to push him over the top, according to his former campaign spokesperson Kevin Liao. “Tom Steyer led an impeachment movement almost 10 years ago now, and I think it's hard to expect the electorate to hold that long of a memory on anything that happened almost a decade ago,” he said. Adam Wren, Kimberly Leonard, Riley Rogerson, Blake Jones and Madison Fernandez contributed reporting.
articles.headline: #Resistance Democrats are flopping in primaries

articles.body: Michael Cohen and President Donald Trump have apparently patched up their differences in private. Now, they can do it in public. The president is scheduled to do a phone interview Thursday with Cohen on the New York City radio show that Trump’s former lawyer and “fixer” began hosting last month. Cohen said in an interview ahead of the broadcast that he and his former boss have met privately three times and reconciled since a bitter and very public falling out during the president’s first term. “I suggest you listen to the show. You may find it extremely interesting,” he told POLITICO. Cohen, who made a stunning conversion from pro-Trump bulldog to fierce critic, said he wasn’t sure if during the interview he and the president would discuss presidential clemency for the conviction that landed him a three-year prison sentence. He isn’t sure he will even push for clemency from the president. “We’ll see,” he said. “Will I make that request down the road? I don’t know. Maybe maybe not.” That the president’s erstwhile attorney is even considering asking Trump for a pardon is somewhat remarkable. Cohen was the star witness in New York prosecutors’ 2024 hush money case against Trump, which saw the then-candidate become the first ever former president to become a convicted felon when he was found guilty on 34 counts of falsifying business records to keep word of an affair with former porn star Stormy Daniels from public view. Cohen, who testified that he lied and bullied for Trump during his years working for the Trump Organization, later turned on his former boss. He told POLITICO in an April 2024 interview, for example, that the Jan. 6 Capitol riot was “grotesque” and predicted “there will never be another election again in America” if he was reelected. Cohen was sentenced to three years in prison in 2018 on charges related to hush money payments to help conceal his boss’ affair with a porn star. He said he sent pardon applications to former President Joe Biden’s administration and the Trump White House but doesn’t consider clemency, which would enable him to recover his law license, critical to his life at this point. “I’m turning 60 next week. What am I going to go start practicing law again?” he said. “What has the loss of my law license prevented me from actually doing? Though I do believe I’m deserving of it, that’s a whole nother story.” Thursday’s interview will mark the culmination of a months-long effort by Cohen to get back in the president’s good graces. He told a New York radio station this summer that they had a text exchange that started their reconciliation. Teasing the interview, Cohen said people will be “interested to hear two individuals that were friends for a decade and a half who have not publicly spoken in eight years” talk about their long shared past. “What could they talk about?” he said.

articles.body: South Carolina Sen. Darline Graham has given opponents fresh ammunition to attack her on her biggest vulnerability: her inexperience. She revealed a major blindspot in her understanding of a critical foreign policy issue, U.S.-Taiwan relations, during Tuesday's debate for the Aug. 25 snap Senate primary runoff to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham. Her response spread like wildfire on social media, with critics saying it proves she is “unprepared” to take office. Asked whether Taiwan and the South China Sea are relevant national security priorities, Graham responded: “I'm just going to be honest here … I'm not that informed on national security, so.” She added that “national security is not my thing, not my area of expertise, but I do support the military.” It was a notable acknowledgement from a sitting senator, as tensions rise between China and Taiwan — and as the U.S. preoccupation with the Iran war calls into question how reliable a supporter it might be amid fears of a possible future invasion of Taiwan. The gaffe exposed the exact weakness that her runoff opponent, GOP Rep. Ralph Norman, has been eager to highlight: the senator’s lack of tenure. His allies immediately piled on. Norman supporter and former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley wrote in a post on X that foreign policy experience is “not something you inherit” — a swipe at Graham’s appointment to fulfill her brother’s current term. Ken Cuccinelli, a former Trump administration official, expressed support for Norman, writing that Graham has “worked hard to hide any firm positions, and here she is at least being honest.” “It very much confirmed many of our suspicions that while she might be a very nice lady, she is woefully underprepared or unprepared to be one of the 100 U.S. Senators in the Senate,” state Rep. Jordan Pace, who is supporting Norman in the runoff, said in an interview. Norman said in a statement that South Carolinians deserve a senator with “know-how” on foreign policy: “Whether it’s spy balloons flying overhead or buying up land near South Carolina military bases, China continues to prove that it is a threat to the United States.” Graham’s campaign, asked to clarify her response on U.S.-Taiwanese relations and her critics’ attacks over her misstep, pointed toward comments she made in the spin room after the debate : “What's important are the people of South Carolina. They're worried about their pocketbooks more than they're worried about the South China Sea, quite honestly.” Graham’s answer is also raising eyebrows among some of her own allies, with less than a week before next Tuesday’s election. And it increases the pressure on President Donald Trump, who had championed Graham’s appointment in July, encouraged her to run for a full term and is even planning to rally with her on Friday to boost her election chances. "[Darline] just doesn’t have the experience of executing, you have to be able to deliver a story about herself and right now her story is that she’s Lindsey Graham’s sister,” said a former Trump administration official, granted anonymity to speak openly about private conversations. The White House is still backing Graham, this person said, because the president had a close relationship with the late senator but also sees her as a better alternative to Norman, who endorsed Haley over Trump in the 2024 Republican presidential primary. A second person familiar with the White House’s thinking, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said, “POTUS is still all in on the endorsement.” The White House declined to comment on Trump’s support for Graham. Still, the flub highlighted the danger for Trump, as he seeks to propel a political novice into a six-year term in the Senate and avoid yet another stain on his endorsement record . His high-profile rally for Graham in Myrtle Beach later this week is a particularly notable step in a year otherwise marked by a decrease in his explicit campaign travel. Norman, for his part, said during the debate that Taiwan is a “definite ally” and that Trump is right to enable them to “defend themselves against China.” He declined to take a swipe at Graham over her comment in real time, but that hasn’t stopped his supporters from hammering the newcomer for the embarrassing misstep. Graham’s stumble was a far cry from her late brother’s hawkish defenses of Taiwan, in which Lindsey Graham had openly criticized the expansionist aims of Chinese President Xi Jinping, called allies of China “dirtbags” and stressed the need to maintain the status quo between Beijing and Taipei to protect U.S. national security interests. “Anyone running for a seat in Congress should be able to explain to the American people why Taiwan is important to American interests. Taiwan is a vibrant democracy of 23 million people and the source of over 90 percent of the world's advanced semiconductors,” said Bonnie Glaser, managing director of the German Marshall Fund’s Indo-Pacific program. “A Chinese takeover by force would shatter U.S. credibility with its allies across the Indo-Pacific.” American intelligence has long suggested that China’s People’s Liberation Army will be sufficiently capable of seizing the island starting in 2027. Trump in June said he was open to speaking with Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te, despite China’s warnings against doing so, in what would be the first direct dialogue between American and Taiwanese leaders in decades. But the U.S.’ war with Iran is casting doubt on how effective an ally the Trump administration will be if China does invade Taiwan. Extended naval deployments to support airstrikes against Iran and a corresponding blockade of its ports have left the U.S. without a deployed aircraft carrier in the Indo-Pacific, as the USS George Washington steams toward the Middle East to relieve the extended Abraham Lincoln carrier, for instance. The heightened risks and the rapid race to replace Lindsey Graham have left some in South Carolina’s GOP circles feeling less than optimistic about the choice they have to make to select a key proxy in Washington. “It was shocking how we're gonna give someone who was on stage last night six years in the U.S. Senate, and I think that’s the overall impression people are having today” said one South Carolina-based Republican operative who has stayed neutral in the Senate race and was granted anonymity to speak candidly. “One of these two is gonna get six years in the Senate? Like, big hanging question mark.”

articles.body: Republicans are struggling to reverse the damage President Donald Trump’s immigration agenda has done with voters. With less than 90 days until the midterm election, the Trump administration has sought to keep Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials out of the headlines , pulling back on the high-profile, flashy raids in blue cities and minimizing public clashes with community members and protesters. But new results from The POLITICO Poll show that half of Americans, including nearly a quarter of Trump’s 2024 voters, still say the president’s mass deportation campaign is too aggressive. That’s virtually unchanged from polling numbers in January and April, amid mounting political outrage over federal agents killing two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis. Non-MAGA Trump voters are twice as likely as self-identified MAGA voters to say the president’s mass deportation campaign is too aggressive — 31 percent compared with 15 percent, according to the new poll, which was conducted Aug. 8 to Aug. 12. The persistence of that negative voter sentiment underscores a vulnerability for Republicans heading into November, as the party grapples with its message and policy approach on an issue the GOP once dominated. Immigration was a reliable winner for Republicans, with the party rallying voters around border security and public safety. Now, they’re struggling not only to convince persuadable voters, but also hold together their own coalition as it splinters over deportations. “Voters really did want border security, but they did not want to see abuelita taken away because she's been here for 40 years but without documentation,” said Arizona-based GOP strategist Barrett Marson. The poll, conducted by London-based polling firm Public First, found a notable share of Americans believe the administration has shifted how it is conducting deportations following the fatal shootings, but that has not been enough to reverse Americans’ views of the administration’s deportation strategy. A 56 percent majority of Americans say there has been at least a small shift in the way the Trump administration has been conducting its deportation campaign. But a plurality of those respondents, 44 percent, say the shifts have made no difference in how much they trust the administration on immigration. Thirty percent say the shifts make them less willing to trust the administration on immigration. Among the 71 percent of Trump voters who said they’ve observed at least a small shift from the administration, nearly half, 48 percent, say those shifts make “no difference” in how much they trust the administration on immigration. Nineteen percent said the shifts make them less likely to trust the administration, while 29 percent said they’d be more likely. Whit Ayres, a Republican pollster in Washington, said that even with the lower-profile approach, the administration’s goal of increasing arrest and deportation numbers remains. That conflicts with what many voters broadly support: targeting immigrants in the country illegally who have committed crimes. The lack of a change in voter sentiment is “not that surprising at all,” Ayres said. “It’s a lot easier just to go into an airport and find somebody who had overstayed a visa, had applied for an extension … and throw them into handcuffs and put them in a detention center. That’s the easy way to get the numbers up, and a great way to thoroughly antagonize public opinion.” Another Republican strategist, granted anonymity to speak candidly about the landscape, said Trump “ran on border security, and he’s following through.” “But the visuals of wins are unfortunately overshadowed by the visuals of chaos,” the strategist said. “There’s no question that the wall to wall coverage of the chaos that follows ICE makes voters squeamish.” The White House pointed to polling from this spring that showed that 80 percent of Americans support deporting unauthorized immigrants who have committed crimes, as well as a Department of Homeland Security press release that highlighted arrests of immigrants who had been accused of sexual assault of a child, forcible sexual abuse and drug posession. “Americans sent President Trump back to the White House with a clear mandate to deport criminal illegal aliens. Every single day the Trump Administration is delivering on his promise to the American people to remove murderers, pedophiles, rapists, and gang members from American communities,” said White House spokesperson Lauren Bis. “Americans are grateful to the President for removing these criminals from their neighborhoods and for Making America Safe Again.” The GOP’s stronghold on immigration as a campaign issue eroded soon after the president’s return to the White House. Soon, robust enforcement efforts led to viral images of arrests inside courthouses, at airports and on neighborhood streets. The backlash brewed for months, and peaked this year amid the killings of Alex Pretti and Renée Good in Minnesota. The White House moved quickly to contain the political fallout, sidelining then-Border Patrol commander Greg Bovino and deploying border czar Tom Homan to ease tensions. The administration has since sought to avoid controversy on immigration ahead of the midterms, emphasized criminal arrests and changed leadership at the Department of Homeland Security. Since Markwayne Mullin took the reins in March, he has reversed contentious policies, including a plan to turn massive warehouses into detention facilities. Still, some Republicans are particularly worried that the hardline immigration stance was hurting the party with key voting blocs, such as young voters, moderate Republicans and Latino voters. The president won 46 percent of the Latino vote in 2024, the highest share of any GOP presidential candidate in modern history, but these voters have grown increasingly concerned with Trump’s deportations policy. Democrats, meanwhile, are highlighting the Trump administration’s aggressive tactics on the trail, betting that more voters are repulsed than grateful for the increased presence of ICE and other federal agents in their communities. Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, who won the Democratic primary for Senate last week, used her victory speech to rail against her opponent, GOP nominee Michele Tafoya. “Michele Tafoya was all in with Trump when ICE was terrorizing our neighbors,” she said. Republicans, for their part, are fractured over the path forward, as immigration hawks battle with wary moderates who are pushing for a targeted focus on criminals. Not only are non-MAGA voters more likely than MAGA voters to say Trump’s mass deportations campaign is too aggressive, there’s also a stark divide in how each faction supports the goals and implementation of his immigration agenda, The POLITICO Poll found. Nearly two-thirds of MAGA Trump voters — 64 percent — say they support both the goals and implementation of his deportations campaign, compared to just 35 percent of non-MAGA Trump voters. The president’s MAGA supporters and immigration hardliners have argued that the administration is going soft on the president’s mass deportation vow, potentially turning off the far right base at a time when the party can’t risk a lull in turnout. The split flared up last month when Mullin temporarily paused some ICE vehicle stops — a tactic the agency was using to increase arrest statistics — after two ICE-involved shootings during vehicle stops in Texas and Maine. While some Republicans welcomed Mullin’s response, the president’s MAGA supporters portrayed it as weak. “We are being betrayed in real time,” conservative commentator Tomi Lahren said on X at the time . “If you want Trump voters to stay home in November, keep this up Markwayne and co.” The president, after online pushback, reversed the DHS order.

articles.body: Barcelona acollirà la Media Party , la conferència internacional de la innovació en periodisme i tecnologia , del 7 al 9 de setembre . Aquesta serà la primera edició d’aquest esdeveniment que s’organitza a Europa, després de 15 trobades organitzades als Estats Units i a l’Argentina. Aquest debut europeu de la Media Party es farà al CaixaForum , amb una agenda centrada en temes com l’autenticitat informativa , la intel·ligència artificial generativa , la verificació de notícies , els models de negoci o les eines digitals per a creadors i redaccions. El congrés és gratuït però cal fer una inscripció prèvia per assistir-hi. També et pot interessar Més de 17.800 persones ja han visitat l’exposició “Tecnologia [in]visible”, al Palau Robert Redacció 1 minut de lectura Crida als periodistes i comunicadors Com en les altres edicions, Media Party convoca els professionals en el camp de la informació i de les noves tecnologies als mitjans de comunicació: periodistes, desenvolupadors, dissenyadors, gestors de producte, investigadors, responsables de polítiques públiques, organitzacions cíviques i líders de mitjans. Amb tot, CaixaForum es convertirà durant tres dies en un laboratori de conferències magistrals, tallers pràctics, espais de treball col·laboratiu i fira de projectes. També et pot interessar Barcelona crearà una unitat per combatre les notícies falses a les xarxes socials Marta Casals Torres Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura Ponents en IA i verificació de fets Per ara, alguns dels ponents ja confirmats són Clara Jiménez (cofundadora de la fundació Maldita.es), Nic Newman (investigador de la Universitat d’Oxford) o Teresa Mondría (experta en aplicar IA en redaccions). En aquesta edició, la Media Party compta amb el suport del Col·legi de Periodistes de Catalunya, el Centre Internacional de Periodistes (ICFJ) i Free Press Unlimited, entre altres organitzacions. L’ambaixadora de la trobada a Barcelona és la periodista Clara Soteras , consultora de mitjans, especialitzada en SEO i creixement d’audiències i que va ser editora de continguts digitals de betevé. articles.body: La previsió del temps per a aquest divendres, 21 d’agost , ve marcat pel tant esperat canvi de temps. Atenció perquè haurem d’estar atents a la possibilitat d’alguns aiguats i, sobretot, a la normalització , lenta, de les temperatures. Previsió horària per a Barcelona : 6 h: paraigua preparat a la bossa 9 h: ambient menys càlid i núvols baixos 12 h: creixement de nuvolades 15 h: probabilitat d’algun xàfec 18 h: ambient més agradable i ruixats 21 h: nit i matinada amb aiguats forts També et pot interessar Per la mare de Déu d’agost, a les set ja és fosc? Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo Marcos Amores Sánchez 2 minuts de lectura Divendres insegur, amb aiguats nocturns i calor suportable L’arribada d’un tàlveg d’aire fred en altura , marcarà un canvi atmosfèric important . De fet, les properes hores passarem de tenir uns 26 ºC a 1.500 m a uns 14 ºC , que, combinat amb la calor acumulada i un mediterrani com un brou, pot propiciar moments d’aiguats intensos. Tot i que al llarg del dia la variabilitat serà la clara protagonista, amb moments de clarianes algunes nuvolades , serà durant el migdia i la tarda quan podrien créixer nuvolades i deixar alguns primers ruixats . Ara per ara, però, els nous models marquen el gruix de la pluja entre el vespre d’aquest divendres i la matinada de dissabte , quan alguns acumulats podrien ser destacables, amb calamarsa, pedra i alguna ratxa forta de vent. Tenim un mar ben calent i un atmosfera ben carregada de calor després de viure un juliol i el que va d’estiu de rècord a Barcelona i molts punts de Catalunya. Això implica molta energia per a les tempestes que, especialment durant la matinada d’aquest dissabte, podran ser localment torrencials entre el sud de la costa central i nord de la costa daurada . Tot i que el gruix de les pluges podrien no afectar de ple Barcelona, sí que podrien comportar enrenou de llamps i trons i alguna complicació cap a l’aeroport del Prat. Tot plegat, caldrà seguir-ho amb atenció al llarg del dia, però us recomanem no deixar el paraigües a l’armari i portar-lo a sobre. Pel que fa a les temperatures , que és el gran desig col·lectiu, notarem una davallada important sobretot de les màximes amb valors que no haurien de pujar més enllà dels 28 o 29 ºC. I les mínimes ? Doncs sí, podem anunciar que en els dies que venen es dormirà clarament millor , amb pocs valors tòrrids aquest divendres que desapareixeran del tot de cara al cap de setmana. Per tant, farà calo r, però la que toca , sense excessos. La inestabilitat no ens abandona Després d’un dijous de forts aiguats cap al País Valencià , el divendres serà el torn de Catalunya , amb tempestes a la meitat nord i est del territori i, al tard, cap a punts de la Costa Daurada. Al llarg del cap de setmana , les temperatures es mantindran ben agradables , amb màximes que els costarà superar els 30 ºC i, el més important, amb les millors nits per dormir, probablement, des que ha començat l’estiu. La inestabilitat no acabarà de desaparèixer , amb alguns xàfecs al prelitroral tant dissabte com diumenge que sembla que podria, de nou, generalitzar-se de cara a dilluns i la setmana vinent.
articles.headline: Arriba el desitjat canvi de temps: amb una calor més suportable i alguns aiguats

articles.body: (ACN) Una nova combinació de fàrmacs millora el control del càncer renal avançat . Així ho indiquen els resultats de l’assaig clínic internacional de fase III LITESPARK-011, publicats a The Lancet . L’assaig inclou 747 pacients amb carcinoma renal avançat de cèl·lules clares que tenien un tumor que havia progressat després de rebre immunoteràpia. Els resultats demostren que la combinació dels fàrmacs belzutifan i lenvatinib millora el control del càncer renal avançat de cèl·lules clares en comparació amb cabozantinib, un dels tractaments estàndard utilitzats actualment en pacients prèviament tractats amb immunoteràpia. Concretament, l’estudi demostra una reducció del 30 % del risc de progressió de la malaltia o mort en comparació amb Cabozantinib. 150.000 morts al món Segons dades del Vall d’Hebron Institut d’Oncologia (VHIO), l’any 2022 es van diagnosticar més de 430.000 casos de càncer renal i aquesta malaltia va causar més de 150.000 morts arreu del món. La forma més freqüent d’aquest tumor és el carcinoma renal de cèl·lules clares , que representa aproximadament quatre de cada cinc casos. En prop del 20 % dels pacients, el càncer ja s’ha estès fora del ronyó en el moment del diagnòstic. A més, en aproximadament un de cada tres casos, la malaltia acaba disseminant-se fins i tot després de la cirurgia. Una combinació de tractaments La Dra. Cristina Suárez, del VHIO i oncòloga mèdica de l’Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron, explica que la majoria dels pacients amb carcinoma renal de cèl·lules clares reben inicialment immunoteràpia. El tractament més habitual, el cabozantinib, és un inhibidor de tirosina-cinasa que bloqueja el creixement dels vasos sanguinis que alimenten el tumor. Tanmateix, afegeix, els pacients amb un càncer renal avançat que progressa després de la immunoteràpia disposen de poques opcions terapèutiques i “sense un estàndard clarament definit”. També et pot interessar Un estudi revela que les dones tenen la meitat de possibilitats de sobreviure a una aturada cardíaca Emma Monrós Rosell 2 minuts de lectura L’estudi, però, es fixa en una nova combinació de fàrmacs que millora el control de la malaltia : belzutifan i lenvatinib. Belzutifan actua inhibint la proteïna HIF-2 alfa, implicada en el creixement i la supervivència de la majoria dels tumors renals de cèl·lules clares. Per la seva banda, lenvatinib també bloqueja la formació de vasos sanguinis que alimenten el tumor. Aquesta doble estratègia busca dificultar el creixement tumoral actuant sobre diferents vies biològiques. Més de 700 pacients L’estudi va incloure 747 pacients amb carcinoma renal avançat de cèl·lules clares el tumor dels quals havia progressat després de rebre immunoteràpia basada en inhibidors dels punts de control immunitari. Els participants es van distribuir en dos grups: 371 pacients van rebre la combinació de belzutifan i lenvatinib, mentre que 376 van ser tractats amb cabozantinib. També et pot interessar Cada cop més a prop d’una vacuna eficient contra el càncer de pell redacció web 1 minut de lectura Després d’un seguiment mitjà de prop de 29 mesos, els investigadors van observar que la combinació experimental aconseguia millors resultats en diversos indicadors clau. El tumor es va reduir o va desaparèixer en el 53 % dels pacients tractats amb belzutifan i lenvatinib, en comparació amb el 40 % dels que van rebre cabozantinib. La supervivència lliure de progressió mitjana, és a dir, el temps que transcorre entre l’inici del tractament i el moment en què el tumor torna a créixer, va ser de 14,8 mesos en els pacients tractats amb la combinació experimental, davant dels 10,7 mesos en el grup tractat amb el tractament estàndard, cosa que representa una reducció del 30 % del risc de progressió o mort . D’altra banda, tot i que la supervivència global va mostrar una tendència favorable per a la combinació (34,9 mesos davant de 27,6 mesos), les diferències no van assolir significació estadística, de manera que serà necessari un seguiment més prolongat.

articles.body: El Barça afronta una temporada amb canvis importants a la plantilla, començant per la capitania . Després de la sortida d’ Alexia Putellas , l’encarregada de lluir el braçalet de primera capitana serà Patri Guijarro . L’acompanyaran, en aquest ordre, Marta Torrejón, Irene Paredes, Aitana Bonmatí i Graham Hansen . Les blaugrana començaran la temporada el diumenge 30 d’agost amb el debut a la Lliga F a casa, al Johan Cruyff , davant el Tenerife. Una capitania merescuda per a una líder nata del vestidor Tot i no portar el braçalet de capitana, Patri Guijarro ja era una líder al vestidor. Vesteix de blaugrana des de l’any 2015 i s’ha convertit en una peça clau al mig del camp del Barça . En una peça indispensable perquè l’equip funcioni molt a prop de la perfecció. Ha estat clau per a la consecució de les quatre Champions que té el club blaugrana al palmarès i amb 28 anys és un mirall en què les joves promeses volen mirar-se. articles.body: Per viatjar no sempre cal agafar el cotxe, el tren o l’avió. Una bona lectura o una pel·lícula ambientada en la destinació somiada ens poden traslladar ben lluny. I una altra manera de fer-ho és a través de la gastronomia . A Barcelona estem de sort, perquè podem fer una ruta per les cuines d’arreu del món sense moure’ns . Cuina romanesa, georgiana, dominicana, vietnamita, africana, cambodjana, salvadorenya, calabresa, iraniana o de l’Uzbekistan explicada pels nous barcelonins al programa B de gust , de betevé. Posa’t còmode i bon viatge! El plat nacional de l’Uzbekistan a Vilapicina Encetem la ruta a l’Àsia central i descobrim la cuina uzbeka al restaurant Samarkand (Santapau, 23). Plats acolorits i perfumats que ens remeten a la mítica ruta de la seda. El plat nacional del país és el plov , que porta  arròs, verdures, hortalisses, llegums i carn de vedella . El cuina amb ofici, paciència i estima  Dilora Babaeva en un local humil al barri de Vilapicina. També et pot interessar Bachata Rosa, simpatia i gastronomia dominicana a dojo a Sants-Badal Bea Rodríguez 3 minuts de lectura Cuina calabresa a Collblanc Tomàquet, alfàbrega, albergínia i picant. Són els ingredients que defineixen la cuina de Calàbria i que impregnen els plats que podrem tastar a De Angelis (carretera de Collblanc, 48). Cuina casolana plena de gustos intensos en aquesta casa liderada pels germans Daniele i Gianluca  de Angelis. Un dels plats que no et pots perdre són els filei alla calabrese , una  pasta casolana  feta amb les barnilles dels paraigües —que porten des d’Itàlia— amb tomàquet, crema d’albergínia, salami picant semicurat, tomàquet sec, formatge de cabra i  nduja  (sobrassada picant). La parmigiana della mamma Laura   (albergínia servida a làmines amb pernil dolç, mozzarella, tomàquet i ou dur) o el  bacallà a la mostassa , amb cebes de Tropea i reducció de mostassa i mel són dues delicadeses més de la carta. 40 anys de cuina cambodjana a la Salut Des del 1992 en una cantonada assolellada del barri de la Salut (Mare de Déu de la Salut, 75) la Kav Ly prepara plats cambodjans i xinesos al restaurant que porta el seu nom. La cuina cambodjana és  refrescant  i  aromàtica , amb molta menta,  galanga  (tija de gust semblant al gingebre) o citronella , i espècies com la  cúrcuma , el  curri vermell  i la  soja  fermentada. També et pot interessar El “bibimbap”, el plat coreà de cinc colors que atrapa per la vista, el gust i l’oïda Bea Rodríguez 3 minuts de lectura El  plat nacional  de Cambodja és el  lok lak , una proposta senzilla amb una base de  llom de vedella assaonat  amb salsa de  soja fosca  i oli, saltat a la paella que se serveix acompanyat d ‘arròs  blanc, enciam,  menta , cogombre i una salsa feta amb  suc de llima , sal i pebre negre. A la carta també hi ha l’ amok , amb  peix  de riu adobat  amb citronella, cúrcuma, galanga i curri vermell, i tampoc no hi falten la crep cambodjana (sense gluten), els rotllets i les crestes fetes amb farina d’arròs al vapor. lok lak Abarka: Difondre la cultura africana a través del menjar Ens traslladem a Sants per viatjar als països de la costa oest africana: el Senegal, Gàmbia, Mali o Costa d’Ivori amb el restaurant i cooperativa Abarka. Ubicat al carrer  Guadiana, 28 , el propietari, Malamine Soly , destaca el  thieboudienne , el plat nacional del Senegal que ha estat declarat  Patrimoni Cultural Immaterial de la Unesco . Una recepta que inclou moltes  verdures  i  peix i que en les àrees de parla wòlof   es consumeix cada dia de l’any. Pierogi ruskie , el plat típic de Polònia A les Corts fa vuit anys que va obrir el Polka Bar. Kamil Ostrowski recorda que va ser pioner a la ciutat i ho va fer amb el propòsit de ser una finestra de la cultura polonesa. Per això quan li demanem que ens triï una recepta ens recomana els pierogi ruskie el plat més típic de  Polònia . Són unes  crestes  de pasta de blat  bullides  que provenen de l’antiga regió de Ruthania —actual Ucraïna— i que al Polka Bar (Cabestany, 7) fan de forma  artesana . “A vegades els millors plats són els més simples”, explica Ostrowski d’aquest plat a base de patata, mató i ceba caramel·litzada. També et pot interessar La Güerita Mexicana, el temple del taco al pastor a Barcelona Bea Rodríguez 2 minuts de lectura El restaurant georgià que omple d’espècies Sant Andreu Coneixes la gastronomia georgiana? Un bon lloc per tastar-la és el restaurant Iberia  (passeig de Fabra i Puig, 96). A la cuina caucàsica hi predominen la  carn , de vedella i de porc, el  formatge  i les  verdures , però sobretot les  espècies pròpies  d’aquest país de l’Europa de l’est, com el  kmeli suneli  (una barreja aromàtica que inclou el coriandre, el fenigrec, l’anet i el marduix) i el  gitsruli  (comí salvatge), originari de les muntanyes de Geòrgia. Fa sis anys que la Mzia Tepnadze i la Khatuna Kureni es van conèixer i van decidir obrir l’Iberia, amb un menú de migdia de plats mediterranis.  El plat nacional de Geòrgia són els  khinkali , uns  saquets de pasta feta a mà ,  farcits  de  carn i espècies , que es fan bullits i es mengen  amb la mà  amb certa delicadesa per degustar a poc a poc el  caldo  que hi queda dins. També et pot interessar “Pupusas”, l’emblema rodó d’El Salvador que es menja amb els dits Bea Rodríguez 2 minuts de lectura La cuina de les àvies romaneses El nom d’aquest local de  cuina tradicional romanesa  al barri de  Sants  no enganya: La Mama Acasa (Guitard, 41). La seva carta es basa en els  plats  que sempre han cuinat les  àvies  i les  mares  d’aquest país centreeuropeu, que encara conserva una economia agrícola potent. Cuina  casolana  en què les  sopes  (de tripa, mandonguilles o costella fumada) són el primer plat  imprescindible  de cada migdia, encara que sigui el mes d’agost. Fa 10 anys que La Mama Acasa s’ha convertit en un  racó de Romania  a Barcelona. Aquí es poden degustar plats típics com els  sarmale  ( rotlles de carn i arròs  embolicats amb col fermentada) i els  mici  ( carn picada  en forma de rotlle, que pot ser vedella, porc o ovella cuinades a la  brasa ), acompanyats del complement que és un símbol del país, la  mamaliga  (feta a partir de farina de  blat de moro ). Ajiaco , símbol gastronòmic de Bogotà Al carrer del Clot, 135, hi trobem el restaurant Muysca , un temple on descobrir la millor cuina colombiana. Una gastronomia amb ingredients  ancestrals  com les  patates  (que a Colòmbia es coneixen com a  papas ) i el blat de moro, presents en multitud de sopes, potatges i rostits. També a l’ ajiaco , un àpat  típic  que, segons els colombians, “restaura l’ànima”. L’ ajiaco  és un dels símbols gastronòmics de  Bogotà  i es fa amb  pollastre ,  panotxa  de blat de moro, tres tipus de  patata  (la criolla, petita i groga, que és nadiua de Colòmbia; la  sabanera  i la  pastusa ), ceba llarga,  coriandre  i  guasca , una herba típica del país que hi dona el gust característic a aquest plat. Ingredients que han d’estar un parell d’hores a l’olla fent xup-xup. També et pot interessar Tacos Cordon Bleu: la cuina francesa de carrer es consolida a Barcelona Bea Rodríguez 2 minuts de lectura La cuina de Les mil i una nits El  Rincón Persa  (Floridablanca, 85) , és el primer restaurant iranià que va obrir a Barcelona (i Catalunya), ara fa 25 anys. La gastronomia iraniana combina els  gustos salats, àcids i dolços  amb  espècies  com el  safrà , fruits secs com les  nous  i els  festucs , i fruita deshidratada com l’emblemàtica  zereshk  (nabiu silvestre persa). L’ albergínia  ocupa un lloc destacat entre els entrants del Rincón Persa, amb dos plats com el  kashk  o  badenyún   (albergínies amb salsa de  formatge curat persa , nous moltes i oli de menta) i el  mirza ghasemí  (albergínies i tomàquets  a la brasa , remenats amb ous i herbes aromàtiques). Entre els plats forts del restaurant també destaquen les  broquetes de pollastre, de xai i de vedella , que es couen a la  brasa , amb el foc ben viu. També et pot interessar Bulka, l’únic forn ucraïnès de Barcelona, elabora pa de motlle de sègol de massa mare Bea Rodríguez 2 minuts de lectura Si és dissabte, toca feijoada La  feijoada és un dels plats que representa millor el Brasil. Un plat de cullera que es fa, a foc lent, amb  mongetes negres ,  vedella ,  costella de porc ,  calabresa  (xoriç fumat brasiler),  bacó , all i  chimichurri .  Es menja tradicionalment els dissabtes , en companyia de la família o els amics. Al  restaurant Mi Casa  (carretera de la Bordeta, 26) en serveixen  entre 120 i 150 racions  cada dissabte i també la resta de dies de la setmana per la insistència dels clients habituals, molts dels quals són  brasilers residents a Barcelona , on viuen més de  17.000  persones nascudes al país sud-americà. Se serveix  acompanyada  d’ arròs blanc , rodanxes de  taronja ,  col ofegada  (cuita a foc lent en un recipient tancat),  farofa   (farina de iuca amb bacó i calabresa) i  vinagreta  (tomàquet, ceba, pebrot i vinagre). Es menja barrejant tots els ingredients en un joc molt equilibrat de textures i sabors. 10 plats de 10 cultures que s’expliquen a través de la seva cuina. No hi pot haver un pla més atractiu per a l’estiu que agafar un passaport gastronòmic i marcar-lo amb un segell després de degustar cadascuna d’aquestes propostes.

articles.body: El Barça ha fet oficial la incorporació de Joao Cancelo , després d’uns dies d’incertesa per temes burocràtics. articles.body: Les obres de millora de la Línia 1 del metro per passar les vies de balast a formigó entre Santa Eulàlia i Mercat Nou encaren la recta final, abans del restabliment del servei el 29 d’agost . Aquests treballs han afectat de ple els usuaris, ja que s’ha hagut de tallar el servei entre les estacions de Florida i plaça de Sants entre el 17 de juliol i el 28 d’agost. També et pot interessar Talls al metro de Barcelona a l’estiu: L1, L9/L10, Verdaguer i l’enllaç de Catalunya | MAPA Eva Vial 2 minuts de lectura Vies de formigó amb menys vibracions La principal millora que s’ha executat és la substitució de les vies, que a partir d’ara estan sobre formigó en lloc de balast. El director de Metro Barcelona, David Prat, ha assenyalat es fa aquest canvi perquè la via en balast requereix un manteniment molt exhaustiu perquè la via es pot moure mou més. En canvi, el formigó és més estable i a més permet reduir el soroll, les vibracions i el manteniment. En total, s’han renovat 1.580 metres de vies des de l’estació de Santa Eulàlia fins a Mercat Nou. A banda, s’ha substituït l’aparell de dilatació , que és un element que evita la deformació dels carrils que es pot produir en cas de canvis rellevants de temperatura. Amb el nou sistema, encara que la temperatura canviï, l’aparell és capaç d’absorbir la dilatació i contracció del carril perquè la via continuï en perfectes condicions. També et pot interessar La calor a les zones d’espera sense climatització del transport públic: “L’andana és com la mort” Redacció 6 minuts de lectura Renovació del taller de Santa Eulàlia A més de renovar les vies convencionals també s’han modernitzat les instal·lacions dels taller centenari de Santa Eulàlia . En aquest cas, s’ha actuat sobre les cinc vies de fossat, substituint el balast pel formigó en un total de 510 metres. També s’han canviat els aparells de via d’accés al taller i s’ha substituït la catenària convencional per una altra de rígida . Les obres mobilitzat 170 persones i han comptat amb un pressupost d’11,5 milions d’euros . La presidenta de TMB, Laia Bonet, ha assenyalat que aquestes obres “són un exemple clar del nostre compromís d’invertir en una xarxa de metro cada vegada més fiable, més robusta i preparada per donar resposta a les necessitats de mobilitat de la ciutadania”. articles.body: Un dels autobusos de la Línia D20 ha estat víctima d’un acte vandàlic aquest dimecres a l’avinguda del Paral·lel . Segons l’Ajuntament, algú va llançar una pedra contra el vehicle i es va rebentar un dels vidres de la tercera porta del bus. De moment, no s’ha identificat l’autor o autors del fet , que no ha no ha deixat cap persona ferida . Foto: Nerea Colomé Una de les usuàries que era a l’interior del vehicle ha explicat a betevé que els fets van passar sobre les 19 h i que tan bon punt la pedra va impactar contra el vehicle, el conductor va evacuar els passatgers . De fet, el consistori apunta que l’autobús es va haver de retirar del servei. articles.body: (ACN) La primera tinenta d’alcaldia de l’ Ajuntament de Barcelona , Laia Bonet , ha expressat que la manifestació prevista per aquest dissabte a Barcelona del moviment conegut com a Save Europe Act “no és benvinguda ” a la ciutat. En una atenció als mitjans aquest dijous, Bonet ha remarcat que aquest acte, promogut per simpatitzants i integrants de la iniciativa d’una llei per salvar Europa , porta “idees que són racistes, xenòfobes i que són contràries a la democràcia i la convivència ”. Ara bé, la tinenta d’alcaldia ha recordat que manifestar-se és un dret fonamental i que, en tot cas, les competències per canviar l’itinerari d’un acte similar o per prohibir-lo són de la Generalitat de Catalunya . També et pot interessar Col·lectius antifeixistes criden a “plantar cara” al moviment xenòfob Save Europe Act a Barcelona Redacció 2 minuts de lectura “La diversitat forma part de l’ADN de Barcelona” Bonet ha afegit que la decisió de prohibir una manifestació és molt excepcional i que, quan es pren, es fa sobre la base d’indicis de risc per a persones i els béns. La tinenta d’alcaldia ha insistit que els Mossos d’Esquadra i la Generalitat estan al cas d’aquesta manifestació i que faran la valoració que correspongui. Amb tot, Bonet ha opinat que la “ diversitat ” forma part “de l’ADN de Barcelona” perquè la ciutat, segons remarca, s’ha construït amb persones que han arribat d’arreu del món. Sobre el paper de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona dissabte, Bonet ha detallat que l’obligació del consistori és garantir la seguretat pública al costat dels Mossos d’Esquadra: “Nosaltres estem en això en aquest moment”, ha conclòs.
articles.headline: Bonet rebutja Save Europe Act, però recorda que prohibir-lo és competència de la Generalitat
